📚 SB 122 Reference Material
Resource
	Key Takeaway
	Brad Hinson — SaaS Tax Offset Sales Play
	Deployment eligibility matrix: AAP Self-Managed = exempt, AAP Azure Managed App = likely eligible, AAP Service on AWS = taxable. Competitive plays vs. Chef, Puppet, Terraform Cloud, GitHub.
	Holland & Knight — SB 122 Legal Analysis
	SB 122 redefines "tangible personal property" to include remotely accessed software. Exemptions: custom software, out-of-state use, IaaS/PaaS. $5M self-assessment threshold. Effective January 1, 2027.
	Numeral — SaaS Sales Tax State-by-State
	20+ states already tax SaaS. California joining in 2027. Combined rate: 7.25% state + local = ~8.85% average. Multi-state operations face compounding exposure.
	Red Hat — Ansible on Cloud Responsibilities
	Customer vs. provider responsibility matrix for each AAP deployment model. Key reference for tax eligibility discussions.
	⚖️ SB 122 Eligibility by AAP Deployment Type
Offering
	Deployment
	SB 122 Status
	AAP Self-Managed
	Customer VPC (AWS, Azure, GCP)
	ELIGIBLE FOR EXEMPTION
	AAP on Azure (Managed App)
	Customer VNet
	LIKELY ELIGIBLE
	AAP Service on AWS
	Red Hat Hosted
	TAXABLE (SaaS)

📧 Aris Wong — VP, Worldwide Engineering


Subject: Engineering tax exposure
To: awong@a10networks.com [inferred]
________________


Aris,
SB 122 takes effect January 1 — every SaaS automation tool your San Jose engineering teams rely on picks up an un-discountable 8–10% tax overhead. For a company shipping products built on Red Hat Enterprise Linux, the fix is straightforward.
Red Hat's self-managed automation runs on that same RHEL foundation — inside A10's infrastructure, exempt from the SaaS tax trigger.
•Ansible Automation Platform — self-managed in your VPC, zero SaaS tax exposure on automation workloads
•Event-Driven Ansible — automated security response for Thunder and Defend without remote-access overhead
•Execution Environments — portable automation across cloud and on-prem with no SaaS dependency
For background on the law: Holland & Knight's analysis of SB 122 covers the definitions and exemptions, and Numeral's state-by-state breakdown shows where California fits in the broader landscape.
Amadeus replaced Chef SaaS with AAP — $5.62M in benefits, 257.9% ROI over three years.
Would August 19th work for 15 minutes? If that week is buried, August 26th works just as well.

📧 Michelle Caron — CFO


Subject: Unplanned 2027 overhead
To: mcaron@a10networks.com [inferred]
________________


Michelle,
California's SB 122 adds an un-discountable 7.25–10.75% tax on every SaaS tool A10's teams use — effective January 1. For a company driving 25–30% EBITDA margins, that's unplanned overhead on a line item that was previously tax-free.
A10 already runs on Red Hat Enterprise Linux. Extending to self-managed automation eliminates the SaaS tax trigger entirely — software running in your own infrastructure isn't "remotely accessed."
•Ansible Automation Platform — self-managed deployment, exempt from SB 122's SaaS classification
•Automation Mesh — scales automation across A10's multi-cloud footprint without per-resource SaaS billing
•AIOps + Ansible — consolidates siloed SaaS monitoring tools into one tax-efficient platform
The legal details are worth sharing with your tax team: Holland & Knight's full breakdown of SB 122 covers exemptions, sourcing rules, and the $5M self-assessment threshold. Numeral's state-by-state SaaS tax guide provides the multi-state context.
ARM consolidated from community tools to enterprise AAP on Azure — $12M deal with lower TCO than their DIY approach.
Would August 19th work for 15 minutes on the budget exposure? August 26th works just as well.

Subject:  SaaS tax exposure modeling
To: rhenderson@a10networks.com
Tier: Manager · ~221 words · Peer: Amadeus · Features: Automation Dashboard, Execution Environments, Self-Service Portal
________________
Ryan,
Every SaaS license in A10’s stack — Salesforce, Workday, Oracle — picks up a 7.25% floor tax under SB 122 starting January 2027. For a finance team managing 25–30% EBITDA targets, that’s unmodeled overhead compounding across every renewal. The forecasting alone — variable local rates up to 10.75% across dozens of contracts — adds weeks of unplanned analysis.
A10 already runs Red Hat Enterprise Linux across your Thunder and Defend infrastructure — Ansible Automation Platform extends that foundation as self-managed software in your own environment, exempt from SB 122.
Automation Dashboard  — surfaces automation ROI in real time across business units. Instead of chasing engineering for quarterly cost-avoidance numbers, the dashboard reports time saved, jobs executed, and cost per task — exactly what EBITDA reporting needs.
Execution Environments  — containerized, versioned runtime packages eliminate dependency drift between dev and prod. Fewer unplanned remediation cycles means the cost predictability your forecasting models require.
Self-Service Portal  — business units request and run pre-approved automation without filing IT tickets. Routine operational requests shift out of the engineering queue into a governed model — reducing per-ticket overhead you’re already tracking.
Amadeus replaced their Chef SaaS with Ansible Automation Platform — $5.62M in total benefits, 257.9% ROI, payback in seven months.

📧 Arvind Bhuvaraghan — Sr. Director, Enterprise Info Mgmt
Subject:  Enterprise app tax burden
To: abhuvaraghan@a10networks.com
Tier: Manager · ~227 words · Peer: ARM · Features: Event-Driven Ansible, Automation Mesh, AIOps
________________
Arvind,
When SB 122 takes effect January 2027, every SaaS tool in your portfolio — Salesforce, Workday, Oracle — becomes 7.25–10.75% more expensive. Managing vendor contracts and compliance across A10’s enterprise application stack, that’s a renegotiation exercise across every active SaaS agreement, with procurement and legal pulling in different directions.
A10 already runs Red Hat Enterprise Linux embedded in your Thunder and Defend products — Ansible Automation Platform extends that foundation as self-managed infrastructure exempt from SB 122.
Event-Driven Ansible  — monitors event streams from your enterprise apps and auto-triggers remediation playbooks. Instead of manually responding to Workday sync failures or Oracle integration alerts, rulebooks detect the pattern and execute the fix before a ticket gets filed.
Automation Mesh  — creates a distributed automation fabric across data centers, cloud VPCs, and remote sites. Jobs route through the most efficient path, and if a node drops, the mesh reroutes automatically — consistent management regardless of where your apps run.
AIOps  — correlates signals across Salesforce, Workday, and Oracle to surface anomalies before they cascade. Instead of investigating alerts in isolation per platform, AIOps identifies root cause across systems — cutting mean-time-to-resolution from hours to minutes.
ARM consolidated 10,000 nodes onto Ansible Automation Platform — lower total cost of ownership than their previous DIY toolchain, $12M through Microsoft MACC.
Would August 19th work for 15 minutes to map this against your application portfolio? If that week is buried, August 26th works just as well.

📧 Chris Wayne — Head of IT
Subject:  Vendor consolidation math
To: cwayne@a10networks.com
Tier: Manager · ~237 words · Peer: Amadeus · Features: Ansible Lightspeed, AI Monitoring Agent, Ansible Automation Platform
________________
Chris,
Building out an IT team while SB 122 adds 7.25–10.75% tax to every SaaS tool is a budget squeeze from both directions — headcount rising and software costs jumping simultaneously. Vendor consolidation becomes less optional when the tax applies per-vendor, per-seat, per-contract.
A10 already runs Red Hat Enterprise Linux across your Thunder and Defend infrastructure — Ansible Automation Platform extends that foundation as self-managed software in your environment, exempt from SB 122.
Ansible Lightspeed  — an AI coding assistant purpose-built for automation content. New team members write production-quality playbooks from natural language prompts instead of learning YAML syntax from scratch — cutting onboarding time from weeks to days as you scale the team.
AI Monitoring Agent  — watches automation jobs in real time and flags failures with root-cause analysis before your team opens the logs. Senior engineers stop spending their first hour triaging overnight failures — the agent surfaces what broke and which playbook to fix.
Ansible Automation Platform  — consolidates provisioning, configuration, patching, and compliance into a single control plane. Instead of maintaining separate tools for each function — each with its own SaaS tax liability — one self-managed platform replaces the sprawl.
Amadeus replaced their Chef SaaS deployment with Ansible Automation Platform — $5.62M in benefits and full payback in seven months, with the SaaS dependency eliminated entirely.
Would August 19th work for 15 minutes on the consolidation math? If that week is buried, August 26th works just as well.
